title: “Monks, how is a monk one who does not know forms? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is all form, namely…
content: “Monks, how is a monk one who does not know forms? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is all form, namely the four great elements and form derived from the four great elements. Thus, monks, a monk does not know forms. Monks, how is a monk one who is not skillful in characteristics? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is the fool and the characteristics of a fool, the wise person and the characteristics of a wise person. Thus, monks, a monk is not skillful in characteristics. Monks, how is a monk one who does not remove the eggs of the gadfly? Here, monks, a monk indulges in arisen sensual thoughts; he does not abandon, dispel, end, or destroy them. He indulges in arisen ill-will thoughts … harmful thoughts … evil, unwholesome states that have arisen; he does not abandon, dispel, end, or destroy them. Thus, monks, is a monk who does not remove the eggs of the gadfly.”

title: “Abandon desire, abandon greed — These are the bonds of worldlings. The one with eyes walks the path, Crosses hell and human birth. Eating little,…
content:
“Abandon desire, abandon greed —
These are the bonds of worldlings.
The one with eyes walks the path,
Crosses hell and human birth.

Eating little, moderate in food,
With few wishes, not greedy —
He is without desire, without craving,
Truly at peace.

Having gone on alms-round,
The sage enters the forest,
Goes to the root of a tree,
Prepares his sitting place.

The wise one, meditating,
Delights in the forest,
Meditating at the root of a tree,
Content, he practices his own pleasure.”

title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as unwise attention. For one who…
content: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as unwise attention. For one who attends unwisely, monks, unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline.”

title: Then the Blessed One saw those people in Sāvatthi, mostly intoxicated with sensual pleasures, living as if drunk, attached, lustful, infatuated, bound, and bewitched by…
content:
Then the Blessed One saw those people in Sāvatthi, mostly intoxicated with sensual pleasures, living as if drunk, attached, lustful, infatuated, bound, and bewitched by sensual pleasures. Then the Blessed One, understanding the meaning, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

Blinded by sensual pleasures,
Covered by a net,
Veiled by craving,
Bound by the fetter of heedlessness —
Like fish caught in a net,
They go to aging and death,
Like a suckling calf to its mother.

title: “So too, venerable sirs, the eye is not the bondage of forms, nor are forms the bondage of the eye. Whatever desire and lust arises…
content: “So too, venerable sirs, the eye is not the bondage of forms, nor are forms the bondage of the eye. Whatever desire and lust arises in dependence on both — that is the bondage there. The ear is not the bondage of sounds … The nose is not the bondage of odors … The tongue is not the bondage of tastes … The body is not the bondage of touches … The mind is not the bondage of phenomena, nor are phenomena the bondage of the mind. Whatever desire and lust arises in dependence on both — that is the bondage there.”

title: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, king fights with king, noble warrior…
content: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, king fights with king, noble warrior fights with noble warrior, brahmin fights with brahmin, householder fights with householder, mother fights with child, child fights with mother, father fights with child, child fights with father, brother fights with brother, brother fights with sister, sister fights with brother, friend fights with friend. Having engaged in quarrels, disputes, and battles, they attack one another with fists, with stones, with sticks, with swords. There they meet death or deadly suffering. Monks, such is the peril of sensuality, a mass of suffering visible here and now, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis – simply because of sensuality.”

title: “Though one should rain down golden coins, One’s desires are not satisfied. Little sweetness, much bitterness — Knowing this, the wise one understands.” “The disciple…
content:
“Though one should rain down golden coins,
One’s desires are not satisfied.
Little sweetness, much bitterness —
Knowing this, the wise one understands.”

“The disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One
Does not seek sensual pleasures,
Even heavenly ones —
He delights only in the destruction of craving.”

title: “Monks, one who does not directly know and fully understand everything, not having his mind dispassionate toward it, abandoning it, cannot make an end of…
content:
“Monks, one who does not directly know and fully understand everything, not having his mind dispassionate toward it, abandoning it, cannot make an end of suffering. One who directly knows and fully understands everything, having his mind dispassionate toward it, abandoning it, can make an end of suffering.” The Blessed One spoke this meaning. Here it is said:

One who knows and understands
Everything as everything,
And does not lust for anything anywhere —
Such a one, indeed,
Has fully understood everything
And can pass beyond
All suffering.

title: Then the Venerable Ānanda went to that nun, sat down on the prepared seat, and said to her: “Sister, this body is produced by food,…
content: Then the Venerable Ānanda went to that nun, sat down on the prepared seat, and said to her: “Sister, this body is produced by food, depends on food. Food should be abandoned. Sister, this body is produced by craving, depends on craving. Craving should be abandoned. Sister, this body is produced by conceit, depends on conceit. Conceit should be abandoned. Sister, this body is produced by sexual intercourse, depends on sexual intercourse. Sexual intercourse — the breaking of the bridge — has been spoken of by the Blessed One. ‘Sister, this body is produced by food, depends on food. Food should be abandoned.’ Thus it has been said. For what reason was this said?”

title: Elder Nun Sumedhā: Remember this human body — Compared to a water bubble — Full of misfortunes, Empty, without core — See the aggregates as…
content:
Elder Nun Sumedhā:

Remember this human body —
Compared to a water bubble —
Full of misfortunes,
Empty, without core —
See the aggregates as impermanent!
Remember the many dangers of hell.

Remember the great charnel ground —
Because of continuous rebirth —
Because of fear of crocodiles —
Remember the Four Noble Truths.

The deathless water is here —
Why would one drink a hundred bitters?
All sensual pleasures
Are truly a hundred thousand bitter.

The deathless water is here!
Why would one delight in feverish sensual pleasures?
All sensual pleasures burn,
Seething and blistering.

There are no enemies here!
Why delight in hostile sensual pleasures?
The king of fire, thieves, water, enemies —
Common enemies are many.

Here there is liberation!
Why let sensual pleasures kill and bind?
In sensual pleasures there is killing and binding —
Delighting in sensual pleasures brings much suffering.

A blazing grass torch —
If you hold it and don’t let go, you’ll be burned.
Sensual pleasures are like a torch —
They burn anyone who doesn’t escape.

Do not accept small sensual pleasures,
Abandoning great, expansive happiness.
Do not be like a fish swallowing a hook,
Then later suffering calamity.

Subdue sensual desire within sensual desires,
Like a dog tied with a leash.
Do not let sensual desires devour you,
Like a hungry man devouring a dog.

Suffering is truly boundless,
It causes much mental distress.
You are tied to sensual desires —
Abandon impermanent sensual desires.

Here, there is no aging!
Why pursue sensual desires that age?
Every birth, everywhere,
Is subject to disease and death —

Here there is no aging, no death —
This is the path without aging,
Without death, without sorrow,
Without enemies, without bonds,
Without stumbling, without fear,
Without burning, without falling.

This goal, many have attained —
This goal is the deathless.
Now it should be realized.
If one is rightly attentive,
Without exertion,
One cannot realize it.

This is the cause, the source —
This is the very root —
Endure the Teacher’s word!
This is the first link —
That is Nibbāna —
If we love the Dhamma.

Thus, with faith,
They spoke these excellent words,
Words full of wisdom —
Supreme, ultimate —
They are disgusted with renewed existence —
Through disgust, craving ceases.
